title: The tennis racket theorem
summary: Why a body spins steadily about two of its axes but flips over about the third, and why a spinning top doesn't fall.

steps.title: Spin about the major axis
steps.text:
Every rigid body has three principal axes. This box has inertias 1, 2, and 2.5 kg·m² (the box in the Animation is long along axis 1 and thin along axis 3).

Spin it about axis 3, the axis of largest inertia, with a small wobble. Open the Analyze ▸ Modes tab: the small disturbances are an oscillation, a Wobble (stable). Run it to see it spin steadily.

check.success: A wobble that never grows: spin about the major axis is stable.

steps.title: Spin about the minor axis
steps.text: Now spin about axis 1, the axis of smallest inertia. Check the Analyze ▸ Modes tab again.

steps.title: The intermediate axis
steps.text: Spin about axis 2, the intermediate one. Now the Analyze ▸ Modes tab shows a real eigenvalue pair: one disturbance grows exponentially, a Tumble (unstable), while its partner decays. Its growth rate is ω √((I₂ − I₁)(I₃ − I₂) / (I₁ I₃)) = 4.5 per second.

steps.title: See it flip
steps.text: Run the tennis racket and watch the Animation. A disturbance of only 0.001 rad/s grows until the body flips over, comes back, and flips again, every 5 s, while the angular momentum L stays fixed in space. The Polhode tab shows why: ω follows the crossing of the energy and momentum ellipsoids, which runs from one end of axis 2 to the other.

check.success: Astronaut Vladimir Dzhanibekov saw a wing nut do this in orbit in 1985.

steps.title: A top that doesn't fall
steps.text:
Gravity pulls on a tilted top, but its torque turns the spin axis sideways instead of down: the top precesses. For a fast top the precession rate is about

    φ' = m g l / (I_s ω_s)

which is 2.45 rad/s for this top spinning at 400 rad/s. Run it and compare the Precession rate in the Summary: about 2.5 rad/s, close to the exact steady rate at its tilt (2.52 rad/s, also in the Summary).

check.success: The faster it spins, the slower it precesses.
